To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

multifrequency phase fluorometric data collected on DNA‐ethidum complexes are described accurately by a torsional dynamics model and that the torsional dynamics parameters of the model are found to be in agreement with values reported in the literature.

(1) multifrequency phase fluorimetry is an effective method to measure DNA torsional dynamics and (2) a torsional dynamics model, developed for DNA, is able to describe the fluorescence data of the DNA‐ethidum complex.

the torsional dynamics of the DNA‐ethidum complex can be described by a single‐mode model and that the DNA‐ethium complex is characterized by a single torsional relaxation rate of 1.2×10 ^{6} s ^{−1} at room temperature and by a torsional energy of 0.6 kcal/mol at 20 °C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new experimental and analytical tools for the investigation of DNA torsional dynamics, and with the study of the torsional dynamics of DNA‐ethidum complexes.
the study of the DNA torsional dynamics by fluorescence anisotropy decay.

the torsional dynamics of the DNA‐ethidum complex is a complex and highly nonlinear process, which can be described by a model with a single relaxation mode.

multifrequency phase fluorimetry, in conjunction with the torsional dynamics model, is capable of providing a quantitative and detailed description of the torsional dynamics of DNA‐ethidum complexes in solution.
multifrequency phase fluorimetry, in conjunction with the appropriate model, is a very powerful technique to study the dynamic aspects of macromolecular systems in the frequency domain.
